problem_text:
A logistics coordinator must allocate a collection of archival boxes onto standardized shelving units. The items to be stored are:

* Archive Alpha: occupies 44 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Beta: occupies 30 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Gamma: occupies 39 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Delta: occupies 43 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Epsilon: occupies 66 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Zeta: occupies 30 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Eta: occupies 56 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Theta: occupies 38 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Iota: occupies 39 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Kappa: occupies 61 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Lambda: occupies 64 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Mu: occupies 32 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Nu: occupies 62 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Xi: occupies 50 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Omicron: occupies 44 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Pi: occupies 41 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Rho: occupies 59 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Sigma: occupies 50 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Tau: occupies 58 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Upsilon: occupies 44 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Phi: occupies 70 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Chi: occupies 47 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Psi: occupies 42 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Omega: occupies 36 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive Digamma: occupies 52 linear centimeters of shelf space.
* Archive San: occupies 61 linear centimeters of shelf space.

Each shelving unit has a total usable linear capacity of 100 centimeters. The coordinator must place every archive box onto a shelf, with each box assigned to exactly one unit. The combined linear space occupied by boxes on any given unit must not surpass its capacity limit. The objective is to utilize the minimal possible number of shelving units to accommodate the entire collection.
